# NTDS / Registry Hive Credential Dumping (Composite L2)

**Tactic:** Credential Access (TA0006) · **ATT&CK:** [T1003.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/003/) · [T1003.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/002/)  
**Status:** ⏳ Awaiting first run  
**Data:** `DeviceProcessEvents`, `DeviceFileEvents` · **Platforms:** Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced Hunting, Microsoft Sentinel (MDE connector) · **Production lookback:** 7d  
**Rule:** [`NTDS_Domain_Credential_Dumping_V2.kql`](NTDS_Domain_Credential_Dumping_V2.kql) · **Author:** Ala Dabat

## Minimum truth

> A credential store is copied: ntdsutil IFM, a volume shadow copy or a registry hive save - or ntds.dit / SAM / SYSTEM / SECURITY is written to disk.

## Reinforcement

Staging path, follow-on transfer, multiple dump techniques on one host.

## Known coverage boundaries

Documented cases where this implementation of the technique does not produce the rule's minimum truth. They run on every build and will report when a rule change closes the gap.

- **`test_empire_ninjacopy.yml`**: coverage boundary - Invoke-NinjaCopy reads the raw volume from in-memory PowerShell: no ntdsutil/vssadmin process and no ntds.dit file write to anchor on

## Run it

```bash
python tools/run_tests.py -k credential_access/ntds_credential_dumping
python tools/run_tests.py -k credential_access/ntds_credential_dumping/test.yml --out query.kql   # paste into ADX
```

The rule in this folder is the **lab build**: identical detection logic, with the lookback widened so the 2019-2020 captures fall inside it (production: 7d). See [methodology](../../../docs/methodology.md) for how tests run and what the telemetry can and cannot represent.
